fields.System.Title: INV-7 — Adjustments
fields.System.Description:
Purpose

Correct a stock figure by hand, with a recorded reason and an approval — the most dangerous
operation in the system, made safe by controls.

Scope

In. Adjusting with a reason code, approval thresholds, adjustment reporting, warning when
adjusting reserved stock.

Out. Counting, which posts adjustments through its own controlled path —
[CNT-303](../../stories/CNT/CNT-303-approve-and-post-adjustment.md).

Design notes

An adjustment is a movement to or from a virtual location — VIRT-LOSS or VIRT-GAIN —
so the ledger stays balanced and total quantity is conserved. This is what makes the
conservation invariant testable.

The requester cannot approve their own adjustment. Enforce in the service layer, not the UI.

INV-703 is the important story here, not INV-701. Adjustment volume is a diagnostic. If
it is high, some upstream process is broken — a receiving control, a picking behaviour, a
master data field. Reporting by reason and by user finds the pattern; without it, adjustment
becomes the fix for everything and the causes are never found.

INV-704 closes a nasty gap. Adjusting down stock that is already reserved leaves an order
allocated against stock that no longer exists, and the picker discovers it at the shelf.

Risks

| Risk | Reference |
|---|---|
| Adjustment used to hide a process problem | [doc 05 WF 13](../../../docs/05-workflows.md) |
| Downward adjustment on reserved stock | [doc 09 §4.5](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
| Adjustment without a movement row | [doc 09 §2.2](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
| Approval bypassed in some path | [doc 05 WF 13](../../../docs/05-workflows.md) |
| Adjustment posted twice on retry | [doc 09 §3.2](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
